title: CompoSkill: Compositional Skill Chain Attacks from Individually Scanner-Passing LLM Agent Skills
abstract: arXiv:2608.16246v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Autonomous AI agents tackling Long Horizon Tasks depend on marketplace skills that are certified one at a time: a scanner returns a safety verdict for each skill and declares the ecosystem safe if every package passes. We show that this assumption fails under skill composition. A skill may pass the per-skill scanner individually yet participate in a risky composition when an agent connects its outputs, capabilities, or side effects with those of other scanner-passing skills. This makes skill composition risk a path level property rather than a node level property, explaining why existing skill scanners that inspect individual packages achieve limited interception. To study this threat, we present CompoSkill, a framework that constructs skill composition attacks through a dual attacker system. translated_title: CompoSkill：从单独通过扫描器的LLM智能体技能中构建组合技能链攻击
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.16246v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：自主AI智能体处理长时程任务时，依赖市场上逐个认证的技能：扫描器对每个技能返回安全判定，若每个包均通过，则声明生态系统安全。我们证明，这一假设在技能组合下失效。一个技能可能单独通过逐技能扫描器，但当智能体将其输出、能力或副作用与其他通过扫描器的技能连接时，它可能参与风险组合。这使得技能组合风险成为路径级属性，而非节点级属性，从而解释了为何检查单个包的现有技能扫描器拦截效果有限。为研究此威胁，我们提出CompoSkill，一个通过双攻击者系统构建技能组合攻击的框架。白盒攻击者知晓受害者的已安装技能池，并直接注入显式技能ID序列；黑盒攻击者仅知晓部分信息。
tldr: 本文提出CompoSkill框架，揭示单个技能通过安全扫描器不足以保证安全，因为技能组合可能产生路径级风险，并通过白盒和黑盒攻击者系统构建组合技能链攻击。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes CompoSkill, a framework that reveals individual skill scanner approval is insufficient for safety, as skill compositions can create path-level risks, and constructs compositional skill chain attacks via white-box and black-box attacker systems.
